title: Command palette dock is unstable with frequent crashes

judgment.rationale: The issue already has a ZIP and a maintainer comment that narrows one crash to AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3.dll, but it still does not identify which specific dock extension or action reliably triggers the access violation.
evidence: The issue says Command Palette Dock crashes spontaneously and mentions adding or using extensions such as Simple snippet and To-do list.
A maintainer comment refocuses the issue away from generic Dock instability and records an Application Error access violation in AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3.dll.

Current source in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/AdaptiveCardsConfig.cs and ContentFormControl.xaml.cs shows Command Palette still hosts Adaptive Cards content in several extension/form paths.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact extension/action trigger and fresh crash evidence so maintainers can narrow the Adaptive Cards crash to one reproducible Dock scenario.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix is plausible, but the current evidence still spans multiple Dock and Adaptive Cards entry points and does not isolate one reproducible crash path.

issue_context.summary: The issue began as broad Dock instability, but the live maintainer triage narrowed it to a crash path that surfaces as an access violation in AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3.dll.
known_information: The report is filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store and includes a PowerToys bug report ZIP.
The reporter mentions instability after adding or using extensions, especially Simple snippet and To-do list.
A maintainer comment says other dock-position issues should be treated separately and quotes an Application Error entry for AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3.dll.
inferences: The likely crash boundary is not generic monitor placement but a specific extension or adaptive-card-rendering path inside Dock-hosted content.
The current report is still too broad to choose a safe fix plan because several Command Palette surfaces use Adaptive Cards.
issue_context.analysis: This should stay in needs-information rather than be marked duplicate or design-ready. The maintainer comment is useful because it isolates the crash family, but the issue still needs one more step of narrowing: which extension or action produces the failing Adaptive Cards content, and whether the same crash still occurs on a current build.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/AdaptiveCardsConfig.cs initializes the AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3 host configuration used by Command Palette.
src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/ContentFormControl.xaml.cs still hosts Adaptive Cards form content, so several extension-driven pages can converge on the same renderer.

information_gaps.information: Which specific extension, dock band, or action was active when the crash occurred.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a generic Dock restore failure from an extension-specific Adaptive Cards render path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact extension or band in use when the crash happens, such as Simple snippet, To-do list, or extension gallery.

information_gaps.information: A short numbered repro on a current build that shows how to make the crash happen again.
information_gaps.why_needed: Without a stable trigger, maintainers cannot tell which Adaptive Cards code path to inspect first.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the steps from opening Command Palette or Dock through the action that immediately precedes the crash.

information_gaps.information: A Windows Error Reporting dump or the full Application Error details from the failing run, if available.
information_gaps.why_needed: The issue already has one event-log signature; a dump or full event details can confirm the same crash site and module offsets on a current build.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After reproducing the crash, attach the WER dump if Windows saved one, or copy the Application Error details from Event Viewer for that run.

actions.label: Identify crashing CmdPal extension path

comment.body:
Thanks for the existing ZIP and the maintainer note that narrows one crash to AdaptiveCards.Rendering.WinUI3.dll. To isolate the failing Command Palette path, please provide:

1. The exact extension, dock band, or action that was active when the crash happened (for example Simple snippet, To-do list, or extension gallery).
2. A short numbered repro on a current build.
3. A WER dump if Windows captured one, or the full Application Error details from Event Viewer for that crash.

That will tell us which Adaptive Cards render path inside CmdPal needs investigation.
